categoryNote: Open topology engine. Every logical-processor, core, die and CPU Set identifier is DERIVED at run time from documented OS buffers (GetLogicalProcessorInformationEx core/cache/die relations and GetSystemCpuSetInformation); hardcoded core indexes and CPU marketing-name lists are a build-validation failure (enforced by tools/selftests/Test-NX19.ps1). CPU Sets are the default mechanism; process affinity is a separate, opt-in mechanism restricted to a single processor group. Process scheduling changes are SESSION-SCOPED: they end with the target process, write no registry value and are journaled only for audit (targetType processCpuSets / processAffinity / processPriority). X3D/CCD detection is a best-effort per-die L3 asymmetry heuristic (>2x), never a name list, and is flagged uncertain. No entry in this category makes a performance claim. Design reference: docs/RESEARCH_RECONCILIATION.md adopt register 6/7 and r1-fsosx-xos.md (reference-only; implementation is original NEXTRIX code).

tweaks.name: CPU topology detection & report engine
tweaks.description: Derives the CPU topology from documented OS buffers: cores, SMT siblings, efficiency tiers, dies/CCDs, per-die L3 cache and the logical-processor-to-CPU-Set-ID map.
tweaks.objective: Provide one verified, uncertainty-marked topology model that every later scheduling entry consumes, with zero hardcoded core indexes.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Calls GetLogicalProcessorInformationEx for RelationProcessorCore (0), RelationCache (2) and RelationProcessorDie (5), plus GetSystemCpuSetInformation and the processor-group count. Each returned variable-sized SYSTEM_LOGICAL_PROCESSOR_INFORMATION_EX entry is parsed by a pure PowerShell function over the raw byte buffer: Relationship at +0, Size at +4, PROCESSOR_RELATIONSHIP payload at +8 (Flags bit 0 = LTP_PC_SMT, EfficiencyClass, RelativePerformance/RelativeEfficiency when the OS supplies them, GroupCount at +30, GROUP_AFFINITY array at +32), CACHE_RELATIONSHIP payload at +8 (Level, CacheSize, Type; GroupCount at +38, masks at +40). Global logical indexes are group*64 + bit. Tiers: each distinct EfficiencyClass is a tier; performance ranking uses RelativePerformance when present, otherwise the documented EfficiencyClass direction (higher value = greater performance, PROCESSOR_RELATIONSHIP documentation) and is then flagged uncertain rather than asserted. Role labels are descriptive (P = highest performance rank, E = next, LP-E = lower ranks, Standard when one class exists); raw numeric classes are always reported. Dies come from RelationProcessorDie; each level-3 cache is attributed to the die with the largest logical-processor overlap. X3D is detected ONLY as per-die L3 asymmetry greater than 2x (strict) and is always BestEffort; a single die or missing die data yields NoAsymmetryDetected/NotDeterminable, never a name-based guess. If Add-Type or any API fails, the report returns topologyAvailable=false with the reason and fabricates nothing. Read-only: no process, registry, service or file state is changed.
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX topology report exists; NX03-011/012 and NX17-007 report hybrid/CCD questions as Uncertain until this engine runs.
tweaks.proposedState: A derived report (cores, tiers, dies, per-die L3, CPU Set map, uncertainty list) available on demand and reusable by later entries.

verify.procedure: Report returns readOnly=true and either topologyAvailable=true with a non-zero logicalProcessorCount whose LPs are all present in the CPU Set map, or topologyAvailable=false with an explicit uncertainty reason. X3D shows confidence BestEffort, NoAsymmetryDetected or NotDeterminable - never an unqualified claim.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only diagnostic; no state is written.

sideEffects: One-time in-memory compile of the interop class (Add-Type) on first use.
No configuration, process or registry state is changed.

tweaks.name: CPU Set derivation engine
tweaks.description: Derives per-class CPU Set selections and single-group affinity masks from the topology model and a workload profile, with no hardcoded indexes.
tweaks.objective: Turn the topology report into explicit, reviewable selections that the application entries can apply or refuse safely.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Pure functions over the NX19-001 model. Pools are derived, never assumed: AllLogical; PerformanceLogical (all LPs of the highest-performance tier); PerformancePrimary (the first enumerated LP of each performance core, SMT siblings excluded); EfficiencyLogical/EfficiencyPrimary (lower tiers, E then LP-E); PerformanceDie/NonPerformanceDie (largest/smallest L3 die when at least two dies exist); CaptureReserve (smaller-L3 die, else lower tiers, else a reserve derived as 1/8 of the physical-core count with a minimum of one, taken from the highest-index first threads). ConvertTo-NxCpuSetIds maps global indexes through the GetSystemCpuSetInformation map and returns resolved=false with the unresolved indexes when an ID is missing - an ID is never fabricated. ConvertTo-NxAffinityMask refuses any selection spanning processor groups (documented SetProcessAffinityMask single-group rule on systems with more than 64 processors) and returns the group-relative mask otherwise. Conservative polarity guard: if the topology has multiple efficiency tiers but the OS did not supply RelativePerformance, the P/E ranking is only documented-direction, so Competitive/Streaming use one LP per physical core across all cores and omit the P/E background split instead of risking a wrong placement; the plan states this. Balanced leaves background work unpinned by design; Productivity derives no restriction. Every plan reports restrictive, certainty and uncertainty. Read-only: no process and no registry state.
tweaks.proposedState: A per-profile plan with per-class logical-processor sets, resolved CPU Set IDs, affinity alternatives and explicit uncertainty.

verify.procedure: Plan returns readOnly=true; every rule's logicalProcessors is a subset of the topology's derived LP set; cpuSetIdsResolved is true only when every selected LP exists in the system CPU Set map; affinity.supported is true only for a single-group selection. No process or registry state is touched.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - pure derivation, nothing is applied.

sideEffects: None beyond the topology probe (NX19-001).

tweaks.name: Per-process CPU Set application
tweaks.description: Applies a topology-derived default CPU Set to a running process by image name; session-scoped and journaled for audit.
tweaks.objective: Steer a chosen process (typically the game) with the documented soft-affinity mechanism without persisting or touching the registry.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Resolves the exact image name to at most 16 running processes, opens each with PROCESS_SET_LIMITED_INFORMATION | PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION, captures the existing process-default CPU sets with GetProcessDefaultCpuSets, journals the capture (targetType 'processCpuSets', with processName, pid, original IDs and sessionScoped=true) and only then calls SetProcessDefaultCpuSets. Verification re-reads GetProcessDefaultCpuSets and compares the ID set order-insensitively; on mismatch or call failure the recorded original set is restored (or cleared when the original was empty) and the failure is journaled. If the original capture fails, the function refuses to mutate (no mutation without verified prior state). The ID list must come from NX19-002/010 or a profile plan, is bounded to 32 IDs, and is never fabricated; a group-spanning selection is reported using the documented rule that CPU-set assignments in groups that do not match the thread's affinity mask are ignored. SESSION-SCOPED and honest: the assignment ends when the process ends, is not persisted, does not affect future processes, and writes no registry value. CPU Sets are the default mechanism because Microsoft documents them as soft affinity compatible with power management; the XOS Toolkit README (reference, r1) reports that default CPU sets are tolerated by more anti-cheat software than affinity masks - a reference-reported compatibility note, not a Microsoft guarantee. -WhatIf plans without opening a handle or writing a journal entry.
tweaks.defaultState: The process has no NEXTRIX-assigned default CPU sets; it runs under normal OS scheduling.
tweaks.proposedState: The process default CPU sets equal the derived selection until the process exits.

verify.procedure: The per-process report shows the requested CPU Set IDs as the process default; a re-read of GetProcessDefaultCpuSets equals the selection. Stopping the process ends the assignment (nothing persists).

rollback.procedure: Session-scoped: the change ends with the process. While the process is still running, Invoke-Nx19Rollback restores the journaled original default set (only-if-ours: live state must still equal the recorded modified set). No registry or persistent state exists to roll back.

originalState.method: GetProcessDefaultCpuSets before mutation; the exact ID set (including the empty 'no default sets' state) and the pid are journaled.

sideEffects: Changes which logical processors the process may use while it runs.
No persistence, no registry write, no effect on new processes.
Anti-cheat compatibility is reference-reported, not guaranteed; per-game results vary and no performance outcome is claimed.
documentationSource: r1-fsosx-xos.md (CPU Sets default / anti-cheat note, reference-only)

tweaks.name: Per-process affinity application
tweaks.description: Applies a hard process affinity mask as a separate, opt-in mechanism; single processor group only.
tweaks.objective: Offer the stricter scheduling mechanism where the owner explicitly needs it, without conflating it with CPU Sets.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: This is deliberately separate from NX19-003. Microsoft documents process affinity as a hard mask that is respected above conflicting CPU-set assignments and inherited by child processes; on systems with more than 64 processors the mask must name processors in a single processor group, and the set must be a subset of the system affinity mask. ConvertTo-NxAffinityMask enforces the single-group rule from the derived topology; the function additionally refuses a requested mask outside GetProcessAffinityMask's system mask. The original process mask is captured and journaled (targetType 'processAffinity'), SetProcessAffinityMask is called, and a re-read verifies the mask; failure restores the original. Selection comes from an explicit topology-derived LP list or a profile plan and is never a hardcoded index. SESSION-SCOPED: no registry write, no persistence; the change ends with the process. Because affinity is stricter than CPU Sets, it is opt-in with ExplicitConsent and preset-excluded; the documented anti-cheat caveat (reference-reported in r1: some anti-cheats block or override affinity masks) is stated in the report rather than promised away. -WhatIf plans without a handle or journal write.
tweaks.defaultState: The process runs with the OS-assigned affinity mask (typically the full system mask).
tweaks.proposedState: The process affinity mask equals the single-group selection until the process exits.

verify.procedure: GetProcessAffinityMask for the target pid equals the requested single-group mask; the report records the group and mask. Stopping the process ends the assignment.

rollback.procedure: Session-scoped: the change ends with the process. While it runs, Invoke-Nx19Rollback restores the journaled original mask under only-if-ours semantics. No persistent state exists.

originalState.method: GetProcessAffinityMask (process and system masks) captured before mutation and journaled with the pid.

sideEffects: Hard affinity overrides CPU-set assignments and is inherited by child processes while the process runs.
Selections spanning processor groups are refused, not clamped.
No registry write and no persistence; anti-cheat behaviour is not guaranteed.
documentationSource: r1-fsosx-xos.md (CPU Sets default, affinity opt-in; reference-only)

tweaks.name: Per-process priority policy
tweaks.description: Sets a narrow, documented priority class (Idle / BelowNormal / Normal / AboveNormal) on a named process for the session.
tweaks.objective: Offer the documented priority lever with a deliberately narrow surface that cannot starve system or input threads.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Opens the matching processes with PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION | PROCESS_SET_INFORMATION, captures the current class with GetPriorityClass, journals it (targetType 'processPriority', original class name and numeric value) and calls SetPriorityClass. Verification re-reads the class; failure restores the original. The allowed set is exactly Idle, BelowNormal, Normal and AboveNormal. High and RealTime are deliberately refused: the documented priority-class semantics make them capable of starving system, input and audio threads, and this entry is scoped to a narrow, explainable policy rather than a general priority playground. Selection is per image name, bounded to 16 processes, and nothing is persisted: the class ends with the process and no registry value is written. -WhatIf plans without a handle or journal write. No performance outcome is claimed.
tweaks.defaultState: The process runs at its own priority class (commonly Normal).
tweaks.proposedState: The process runs at the selected narrow priority class until it exits.

verify.procedure: GetPriorityClass for the target pid returns the requested class; the per-process report shows the same value. A process restart returns to its own class.

rollback.procedure: Session-scoped: the class ends with the process. While it runs, Invoke-Nx19Rollback restores the journaled original class under only-if-ours semantics.

originalState.method: GetPriorityClass captured before mutation; class name and numeric value journaled with the pid.

sideEffects: Changes scheduler priority relative to other processes while the target runs.
High and RealTime are refused by design.
No persistence and no registry write; no performance outcome is claimed.

tweaks.name: Scheduling profile: Competitive
tweaks.description: Parameter set for the derivation engine: game on the first thread of each performance core, background work on lower tiers when they exist.
tweaks.objective: Express the competitive intent as data that NX19-002..005 consume, without hardcoding any processor index.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Defined and implemented as data (Get-NxSchedulingProfileDefinition). Parameters: game class id 1 on pool PerformancePrimary (first enumerated LP of each performance core), background class id 3 on pool EfficiencyLogical, no capture pool, priority intent AboveNormal for the game and BelowNormal for background, minimum game logical processors 4. The minimum is a count rule, not an index rule: if fewer than four performance-primary LPs exist, the game pool widens to all performance-tier LPs. If the topology has a single tier, no Background rule is produced and background apps are left unpinned instead of being forced onto game cores. If tier polarity is not OS-derived (no RelativePerformance), the plan avoids P/E-specific pinning and uses one LP per physical core across all cores. The profile applies nothing itself: NX19-002 derives the plan and NX19-003/004/005 apply only when explicitly selected. Trade-offs are stated; no performance claim is made.
tweaks.proposedState: A Competitive plan artifact (read-only) available to the application entries.

verify.procedure: The plan reports profile=Competitive, restrictive=true when the topology has more LPs than the game selection, a Game rule with classId 1, and (only when a lower tier exists) a Background rule with classId 3. Every selected LP exists in the topology.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - profile data and a read-only plan.

sideEffects: Choosing this profile expresses an intent only; nothing is applied until an application entry is selected.
Trade-off: SMT siblings are excluded from the game selection when at least four performance-primary LPs exist.
documentationSource: r3-sapphire-vain.md (per-process class schema Game=1/Background=3; design hint only)

tweaks.name: Scheduling profile: Balanced gaming
tweaks.description: Parameter set that gives the game all performance-tier logical processors while leaving background work under normal OS scheduling.
tweaks.objective: A gaming-oriented middle ground that preserves background responsiveness by not pinning it.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Defined and implemented as data. Parameters: game class id 1 on pool PerformanceLogical (all LPs of the highest-performance tier, SMT included), no background pool, no capture pool, no priority intent, minimum game logical processors 1. The absence of a background rule is the point: Microsoft's scheduler continues to place background work normally, so responsiveness is not traded away. On a single-tier topology the performance tier is every logical processor and the plan is reported non-restrictive. If tier polarity is not OS-derived, the plan applies no P/E-specific restriction. The profile applies nothing itself; NX19-002 derives it and the application entries act only when selected. No performance claim is made.
tweaks.proposedState: A Balanced plan artifact (read-only) available to the application entries.

verify.procedure: The plan reports profile=Balanced with a Game rule and no Background rule; restrictive=false when the performance tier equals every LP. Every selected LP exists in the topology.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - profile data and a read-only plan.

sideEffects: Choosing this profile expresses an intent only; nothing is applied until an application entry is selected.
Background responsiveness is preserved by not pinning background work.

tweaks.name: Scheduling profile: Streaming
tweaks.description: Parameter set that reserves encode/capture capacity away from the game and is explicit about OBS placement.
tweaks.objective: Give capture and encoding their own derived capacity instead of letting them compete with the game on the same cores.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Defined and implemented as data. Parameters: game class id 1 on PerformancePrimary, capture class id 2 on CaptureReserve, background class id 3 on EfficiencyLogical, priority intents AboveNormal (game), Normal (capture) and BelowNormal (background), minimum game logical processors 4. CaptureReserve is derived in this order: the smaller-L3 die when at least two dies exist; otherwise the lower-performance tiers; otherwise a reserve of 1/8 of the physical-core count (minimum one) taken from the highest-index first threads. OBS guidance is data: apply class Capture to the encoder/capture image and class Game to the game, never the Game selection to OBS. If tier polarity is not OS-derived, the game uses physical-core first threads and the capture reserve is the core-count-derived slice. If no reserve can be derived, capture is not pinned and the plan says so. The profile applies nothing itself; no performance claim is made.
tweaks.proposedState: A Streaming plan artifact (read-only) with game, capture and background selections.

verify.procedure: The plan reports profile=Streaming with Game classId 1 and Capture classId 2 rules whose LP sets are disjoint, plus a Background rule only when a lower tier exists. The capture pool's derivation string states its source.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - profile data and a read-only plan.

sideEffects: Choosing this profile expresses an intent only; nothing is applied until an application entry is selected.
Reserving capacity for capture can reduce the processors available to the game on a small topology.
documentationSource: r6-hone-amewizard.md (capture tools protected in session rules)

tweaks.name: Scheduling profile: Productivity
tweaks.description: Parameter set that derives no restriction so every logical processor remains available to every workload.
tweaks.objective: Cover the no-pinning choice inside the profile set instead of forcing a restrictive selection for general use.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Defined and implemented as data. The profile has no game, background or capture pool and no priority intent, so New-NxCpuSetPlan returns restrictive=false with zero rules and an explicit note. This is intentional: a productivity/multitasking machine should not inherit a gaming split, and a no-op profile is preferable to a third-party tool with hidden behaviour. The entry still records the profile so the owner can see that the category was considered and deliberately left non-restrictive. It applies nothing and makes no performance claim.

verify.procedure: The plan reports profile=Productivity, restrictive=false and zero rules, with an uncertainty note stating that no restriction is intentional.

sideEffects: None by design: the profile applies no CPU Set, affinity or priority change.

tweaks.name: Scheduling profile: Custom builder
tweaks.description: Validates user-defined per-process rules (class + explicit LPs or a derived pool) against the detected topology before producing a plan.
tweaks.objective: Let an owner express a per-process schedule while every index is still topology-validated and no rule is invented by NEXTRIX.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Rules use the per-process convention adopted from the reference research (r3 design hint): an exact image name, a class (Game=1, Capture=2, Background=3) and either an explicit logical-processor list or a derived pool name. Validation is pure and returns every issue at once: empty/placeholder names, wildcards, names over 260 characters, unknown classes, duplicate process names (case-insensitive), unknown pools, duplicate LPs, and any LP that does not exist in the detected topology are rejected - never clamped or dropped. Bounds: 64 rules. At least one Game rule is required. CPU Set IDs are resolved from the system map; an unresolved ID makes that rule non-applicable and the plan reports it rather than substituting an ID. The plan is read-only; application happens through NX19-003/004/005. The registry action with no rules returns Rejected by design: NEXTRIX does not ship a hardcoded sample rule, because a sample would be exactly the kind of baked-in index list this category forbids. No performance claim is made.
tweaks.proposedState: A validated custom plan artifact (read-only) for the application entries.

verify.procedure: With no rules the plan reports valid=false and the reason 'At least one rule is required' (no plan, no mutation). With valid rules every selected LP exists in the topology, every rule has exactly one class and name, and at least one Game rule is present.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - validation and a read-only plan.

sideEffects: Nothing is applied by the builder; an invalid rule set produces no plan.
Rules are bounded to 64 and process names are exact, not patterns.
documentationSource: r3-sapphire-vain.md (per-process rule schema Game=1/Background=3; design hint)
r1-fsosx-xos.md (rule validation limits and cross-machine sanity checks; reference-only)

tweaks.name: AMD X3D / CCD-aware placement guidance
tweaks.description: Best-effort, uncertainty-marked guidance on large-L3 die placement, derived only from per-die L3 asymmetry.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner usable CCD guidance without ever asserting X3D from a CPU marketing name.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Consumes the NX19-001 model only. A die is treated as a large-L3 die when its summed level-3 cache is strictly more than twice the smallest positive per-die L3; the result is always BestEffort. With one die, two symmetric dies, fewer than two dies reporting L3, or missing RelationProcessorDie data, the function reports NoAsymmetryDetected or NotDeterminable and offers no X3D-specific placement. The guidance names the derived large-L3 logical processors and suggests, if the owner wants cache-favoured placement, selecting those LPs for a Game rule in NX19-010 while keeping background/capture on the other die - but it applies nothing. It never reads the processor name string, never matches a model list, and never claims a performance outcome. EXPERIMENTAL/E0: the heuristic is a design judgement about cache asymmetry, not a documented Microsoft or AMD contract.
tweaks.defaultState: No X3D/CCD guidance; marketing-name assumptions are not made anywhere.
tweaks.proposedState: Best-effort guidance report with the derived large-L3 die LP set and explicit confidence.

verify.procedure: The report's detection is LargeL3DieAsymmetry, NoAsymmetry or NotDeterminable; when LargeL3DieAsymmetry, largeDieLogicalProcessors is a subset of the topology LPs and confidence is BestEffort. The report contains no claim derived from the CPU name.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - read-only guidance; nothing is applied.

sideEffects: None: guidance text only; any placement must be selected explicitly through NX19-010.
documentationSource: r3-sapphire-vain.md (closed per-core engine rejected as a design model)
